2013_052_090313mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education packet for the regular meeting of September 3, 2013, at 7:00 PM at Athens High School, 4333 John R, combines spring-sports recognitions, three sets of prior minutes, the Treasurer's Reports for June and July 2013 with complete check registers and fund budget statements, probationary contracts for incoming teachers, and reports on summer learning, enrollment and the bond campaign. ## Meeting
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, September 3, 2013, 7:00 PM, Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. Board offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per person.

## Recognitions
Mr. Jolly to read biographies of the spring 2013 all-state athletes (Elizabeth Abro, Nicholas Boynton, Cara Burns, Haley Burns, Kalie Collins, Jay Darish, Brittany Friesen, Amanda Guo, Daniel Harris, Connor Hayden, Sydney Heath, Madison Hirsch, Alison Holland, Gabriella Mancini, Rachel Sacco, Sara Troccoli), followed by the Troy High girls' state soccer champions coached by Brian Zawislak.

## Consent agenda: minutes and bond
Minutes of the August 6, 2013 workshop (5:00 p.m. to 7:18 p.m.), the August 6 regular meeting (7:25 p.m. to 9:08 p.m.), and the August 21 special meeting. Resolutions adopted August 6: 13-073 consent agenda; 13-074 personnel; 13-075 a two-year probationary administrative contract for Ryan Brinks as Associate Principal, International Academy-East, effective August 7, 2013; 13-076 Section 105c Schools of Choice for unlimited 9th graders at IA-East for 2014-2015; 13-077 the School Improvement Bond Proposition; 13-078 MASB delegates; 13-079 closed session. All carried Yes 7 / No 0.

The ballot proposition asks to borrow not to exceed One Hundred Twenty Five Million ($125,000,000) Dollars in general obligation unlimited tax bonds for security-related remodeling, technology equipment and infrastructure, building additions, site work and school buses; not more than fifteen (15) years outstanding; estimated first-year millage 1.84 mills and estimated simple average annual millage 2.93 mills. The District states $93,605,000 of qualified bonds outstanding and $0 of qualified loans under the School Bond Qualification and Loan Program.

## Item 5 — Minutes and August resolutions
August 6, 2013 special workshop, Administration Building: President Philippart convened at 5:00 p.m. with Mrs. Edmunds, Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Miletti, Mr. Schmidt and Ms. Underwood, plus Superintendent Fowler, Ms. Birmingham, Mrs. Keeling, Dr. Machesky and Mr. Witt; topics were TEAM updates, a rubric for performance-based compensation, board/district goals, a bond update and MASB board delegates; adjourned 7:18 p.m.

August 6, 2013 regular meeting, called to order 7:25 p.m. with roughly 15 in the audience; every roll call was Yes 7 / No 0. Resolution 13-073 approved the July 9, 2013 minutes. Resolution 13-074 approved elementary and secondary personnel; Mr. Witt reported 37 new hires with 7 additional new teachers still to turn in paperwork. Resolution 13-075 issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Ryan Brinks as Associate Principal, International Academy-East, effective August 7, 2013. Resolution 13-076 adopted Schools of Choice under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepting an unlimited number of 9th grade students for 2014-2015 at International Academy East from districts in counties contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District; Dr. Machesky reported 148 applications with 52 students qualified in 2012-2013 and 159 applications with 76 qualified for 2013-2014. Resolution 13-078 certified Mrs. Paula Fleming, Mr. Todd Miletti, Ms. Nancy Philippart and Mr. Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2013 Delegate Assembly, October 24-27, 2013. Resolution 13-079 authorized closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c); closed session 7:49 p.m., reconvened 7:55 p.m.; adjourned 9:08 p.m. Minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

## Resolution 13-077 — School Improvement Bond Proposition
The proposition (Exhibit A) goes to a Special School Election on November 5, 2013, certified to the Election Coordinator on or before August 27, 2013, not less than seventy (70) days prior, under the Michigan Election Law, Act 116, Public Acts of Michigan, 1954. Ballot terms: borrow not to exceed One Hundred Twenty Five Million ($125,000,000) Dollars in general obligation unlimited tax bonds to remodel, equip, re-equip, furnish and re-furnish buildings to enhance security; acquire and install technology equipment and technology infrastructure; construct additions; and improve sites plus purchase school buses. Maximum term not more than fifteen (15) years exclusive of refunding; estimated millage in the first year 1.84 mills ($1.84 per $1,000 of taxable value); estimated simple average annual millage to retire the bonds 2.93 mills ($2.93 per $1,000 of taxable value). The bonds would be guaranteed under the School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, against $93,605,000 of qualified bonds outstanding and $0 of qualified loans; proceeds cannot be used for salaries, repair or maintenance costs or other operating expenses. Adopted Yes 7 / No 0, certified by Paula Fleming under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Members discussed Detroit's recent bankruptcy filing and its possible effect on surrounding districts and bond sales.

August 21, 2013 special meeting: Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Schmidt present, Miletti and Underwood participating via remote communications during closed session. Resolution 13-080 endorsed the Common Core State Standards, citing the Michigan State Board of Education's unanimous June 15, 2010 adoption of the CCSS as the Michigan Core Standards for mathematics and English/language arts, warning that legislative budget language barring participation would jeopardize Michigan's No Child Left Behind waiver, and urging the Legislature to fund continued implementation; signed by Nancy Philippart, Board President, and Paula Fleming, Board Secretary. Resolution 13-081 authorized closed session on negotiations, carried 5-0; closed session 5:18 p.m., reconvened 5:20 p.m.; adjourned 7:20 p.m.
